scope: Audit the derivative of the unchanged native JAX-CFD numerical map before considering an independent reference derivative.
required_comparisons: Same public float32 checkpoints and exact physics for native direct recurrence and adapter recurrence; compare forwards before gradients.
Native JVP/VJP dot identity is internal same-AD consistency, not an independent gold standard.
Fixed central and both one-sided finite-difference epsilon sweeps, retaining all results and rejected states.
Float64 scalar reductions of unchanged float32 outputs; report absolute error, objective magnitudes, and realized cast input perturbation.
Projected gradient direction and independent fixed random tangent direction, with identical normalization across epsilon.
Actual neural loss gradient comparison at saved initialization; only use trained checkpoints if original files exist.
interpretation: Adapter/direct discrepancies with identical forward values indicate an integration-path issue worth isolating.
Finite differences converging toward AD before small-epsilon rounding dominates support a truncation/branch-crossing explanation.
One-sided asymmetry can reflect curvature, finite-step branch crossing, or nonsmoothness; it alone does not establish the cause.
A stable FD plateau away from AD in a resolved perturbation regime motivates independent derivative investigation; it does not by itself identify a bug.
Changed native precision or altered limiter produces a distinct numerical map and cannot silently become the reference for the original derivative.
A branch-observing diagnostic must retain native forward arithmetic and report exact source identity; tiny-tail branch counts alone do not establish gradient relevance.
